target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech researchers and academic labs that want to run life science experiments remotely
problem: Wet lab research was slow, labor intensive and hard to reproduce, and small teams could not afford lab space and equipment.
business_model: Usage-based robotic cloud lab services plus on-premise lab software
product_category: Robotic cloud laboratory for life sciences

founders.name: Max Hodak
founders.background_notes: YC page says he did research at Duke Medical Center and later founded Science.

investors: more than 60 accredited investors via AngelList and SecondMarket

exit.reason: Transcriptic merged with 3Scan to form Strateos. The YC directory marks Transcriptic inactive because the brand was replaced.

competitors.name: Emerald Cloud Lab (Emerald Therapeutics)
competitors.what: Robotic cloud lab for running wet lab experiments remotely
competitors.traction_then: Still in testing and not publicly available as of Feb 2015 per TechCrunch; Bio-IT World reported its public launch in July 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a fleet of integrated lab robots with remote protocol execution, reproducibility controls and a web interface required robotics, biology and software expertise that few teams had in 2012.

defensibility.rationale: Capital intense robotic labs and protocol software were hard to copy quickly, and customers integrating through the lab environment faced switching costs, but a funded rival (Emerald) was building the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in a way the sources describe. The company merged with 3Scan in 2019 and the combined Strateos later shifted to on-site cloud labs in April 2023.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2015 reported the company said top pharma and biotech firms were using it, and it described the aim of letting small teams run drug research without large equipment or lab space.

branding.domain_note: transcriptic.com now redirects to strateos.com after the 2019 merger.

rebrands.why: Merger with 3Scan; the combined company took a new name.

branding.community_and_virality: Seed round was publicized as the first significant equity round raised online through AngelList and SecondMarket.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among synthetic biology and lab automation press as a pioneer of cloud labs, but sources show no mascot or consumer brand effort and the name was retired in 2019.

pivots.to: Strateos combining cloud lab with 3Scan tissue imaging
pivots.why: Merger of equals announced as a combined drug discovery technology provider.

outcome_analysis: Transcriptic was an early robotic cloud lab that raised a 1.2 million dollar seed in 2012, an 8.5 million dollar Series A in 2015 and a 13.4 million dollar round in 2016, then merged with 3Scan in June 2019 to form Strateos. The directory Inactive status reflects the brand ending in that merger rather than a documented shutdown. Strateos later announced a shift to on-site cloud labs in April 2023, and no source opened gives final results for the combined company.
notes: The 2016-11 round is labeled Series A-1 by the company per search summaries, so it is recorded as other. Its lead is disputed between sources (Founders Fund participation per Seedtable, Y Combinator named lead there, Matthew Ocko per StartupIntros). The 2014-02 other equity entry rests on a single database with no amount. TechCrunch in Feb 2015 stated total raised just over 14 million dollars, while the rounds recorded to that date sum to 9.7 million, so about 4.3 million is unaccounted for. A source summary names Tim Gardner as a co-founder, but no opened company source says so, so he is not listed. The strateos.com page and the Strateos merger blog post could not be read fully (one returned an error, the home page copy was a stale cache). Strateos shift to on-site cloud labs is from a Business Wire headline in search results, not opened.
